checks: Read ce2469e6ba848252 §§2.2–3, (4)–(5), with the base restriction in §2.1. Minkowski combinations of positive-radius balls make every integer base in conv P positive. Removing bases outside conv P discards any originally null integer fiber from the induction domain.

The lattice chart acts only on base coordinates and preserves integer fibers. Both strict sides have positive mixed mass because every plane with nonzero continuous normal is fiberwise null. Therefore there are relative-interior points on both sides and the section has full relative dimension after shearing.

The shear leaves each base fixed and deletion of the constant height on its section fiber is an isometry within that fiber. Its measure is the ordinary summed (d−1)-volume, including counting for d=1. With a nonunit normal the uniform coarea factor is exactly 1/||u_i||.

The substitution t=b_i−a_i·z gives the displayed oblique restricted margins. At any point missed by all other caps, an arbitrarily small move in −u_i makes the i-margin negative while preserving the strict negative signs of the rest. Thus the other caps cover the section plane, and the one actual lower-dimensional depth witness is in one of them.
All-space restrictions have full measure; an empty restriction cannot contain the witness. The single-point reduced space gives the same bound with gamma_0=1 and m=0.

dependencies.hypotheses: After restricting to the hull of the positive bases, every occupied integer fiber is positive and the occupied base span is aff P. Use the stated saturated chart on that mixed set. The resulting full-dimensional canonical hull is contained in the reduced body, whose section is used here. The chart fixes x and preserves all fiber section measures.

overlap.comparison: Covers affine lattice reduction and preservation of fiber measure on the full-dimensional occupied hull. It gives no cover of the geometric section by other labels and no cross-cap overlap from the lower-dimensional point.

readability: The cap section means the intersection of the reduced body with the plane. The proof clearly distinguishes full geometric trace from a fractional effective trace.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The reduced mixed section and the exact full-trace overlap are valid under the stated lower-dimensional depth hypothesis.
